crime: During several afternoon free periods, {WITCH_NAME} and another girl drew ordinary objects together in the lounge. They took turns choosing a subject, then each drew the same thing. One calm afternoon, they sat by the fireplace drawing the crossbow kept in the lounge. The fire had been burning quietly when a live ember suddenly popped out, burned through the girl's paper, and left a small scorch mark on her sleeve before the girl brushed the ember away. {WITCH_NAME} curled up beside the sofa and went limp, remaining motionless until the room was quiet again. The girl replaced the paper, said no one could have predicted the ember, and promised to return that evening to finish the drawing. “Next time, an unforeseeable accident may hurt you instead of the paper,” {WITCH_NAME} said. The girl replied, “I can't stop living my life just because something might happen without warning.” {WITCH_NAME} decided that a quick death at a time of her choosing was safer for the girl than waiting for an unknown catastrophe.

During evening free time, {WITCH_NAME} was already waiting with her own drawing when the girl returned with the unfinished one. {WITCH_NAME} explained that her picture needed a kneeling figure facing her to show the crossbow's scale, then stood opposite a sofa with the drawing. The girl knelt facing her on the floor directly in front of the sofa, with her back toward the sofa, and agreed to hold the pose briefly. Two prisoners who had arranged to meet the girl arrived together at the lounge entrance. The girl asked them to wait until the pose was finished. From the corridor, they could see each other and anyone crossing the doorway, but not the far side of the sofa behind the girl.

{WITCH_NAME} said her pencil had rolled behind the sofa and went to retrieve it. The girl promised to hold the pose until {WITCH_NAME} returned. Hidden from the girl and both prisoners, {WITCH_NAME} walked around the sofa, said she could not find the pencil and would fetch another, then continued to the doorway. Both prisoners watched her leave. They remained together at the entrance, kept each other in sight, and saw no one enter afterward. Less than a minute later, both heard the crossbow fire inside.

They found the girl dead on the floor in front of the sofa. A bolt had entered her upper back from above and passed through her heart. The crossbow lay on the floor behind her. The top of the sofa back bore two fresh dents. Their spacing matched the distance between the crossbow's stock and fore-end, and the line between them matched the bolt's path. The catch holding the bowstring was intact, and no cord, weight, or other object was attached to the trigger.

The dents and wound path showed that the crossbow had been braced on the far side of the sofa back, above and behind the victim, and aimed down at the spot where the victim had knelt. Recoil had knocked it to the floor. The victim could not have reached the trigger behind and above her from that kneeling position. The two prisoners recocked the crossbow without a bolt; its catch held securely and released only when the trigger was pulled, ruling out an ordinary delayed malfunction.

While the lounge was empty before the girl arrived that evening, {WITCH_NAME} loaded the crossbow, braced it on the sofa back, and kept its trigger perfectly still for less time than the planned pose would last. That promise kept the girl beneath the aimed crossbow longer than the stored interval. Behind the sofa, {WITCH_NAME} tried to pull the trigger, but it stayed still. She then left under the pretext of fetching another pencil. Because both prisoners had watched the doorway and each other, no one could have entered to pull the trigger after she left. When the stored interval ended, the trigger completed the pull {WITCH_NAME} had attempted and released the catch. The crossbow fired the bolt through the girl's back and heart, killing her.
fields.epitaph: She chose the hour disaster would come, never knowing it had taken all the hours before.
execution: A large horizontal iron drum appeared on the execution stand. Its inner wall was rough and both ends were sealed, but the circular end facing the audience was transparent, leaving the entire interior visible.

She curled up at the bottom and tried to remain still. The drum began to rotate. Its rough wall carried her upward, then dropped her back onto the bottom. Each turn lifted and dropped her again. As the drum accelerated, her body could not settle.
Her shoulders, back, ribs, arms, head, and neck struck the iron wall again and again. The impacts broke her ribs and neck and caused fatal head trauma. The drum continued to turn after she died.

magic.name: Deferred Motion
magic.text: She can store a movement in an object and make the object complete it later.
